messages.author: 9d945ece5517d9b7
messages.subject: Mitochondrial DNA analysis
parts:
Hi,

Do you have suggestions for analysing CNVs from mitochondrial DNA with CODEX? I have files from targeted sequencing for mitochondrial DNA. For now I keep running into errors, and try to solve them one by one. The latest I couldn't solve, from the getmapp.R function 

"Error in mappability[[chrtemp]] : subscript out of bounds"

I see that chrX is assigned as 23 and chrY as 24. Could chrM be assigned just as 25? The mitochondrial DNA is in the reference as chrM, the same as in my BAM file headers, but it doesn't seem to be enough.... What should be changed?

I have successfully used CODEX for targeted gene panel analysis, and I like it very much and would like to be able to continue doing analysis with it.

Best regards
Salla Välipakka

messages.author: 94ec915e8ce36448
messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] Mitochondrial DNA analysis
parts:
Hi Salla,

Thanks for your interest in CODEX. This is the first time I got an email asking about application of CODEX to mt genome, which is interesting and I hope CODEX can be of help.
For CODEX, we pre-calculate all mappability for the autosome and sex chromosome since it can be time-consuming.
For your case, you can set all mappability to 1. That is, mapp=rep(1, length(gc)) after calculating the GC content. The mappability is only used in the QC step and thus this should not affect your final output.

What you need to be careful about is the calculation of the GC content since this is used as input for normalization to get the GC content bias. I recommend some sanity check and zooming in the the function getgc(), which is very short to read.

Let me know if you have further questions.
Yuchao

messages.subject: Re: [codex_wes_cnv] Mitochondrial DNA analysis
parts:
Hi Salla,

I had a typo in my previous email. I meant there might be something wrong with your code. See below for my response to your previous questions.

“How do you propose the mtDNA regions should be divided in the probes file?” I don’t have a direct answer since I haven’t analyzed mt CNV before and am not sure what a good bandwidth for the bins should be. Also I don’t understand what you mean by “ I think the problem may be with the probes file I use - the thing is I didn't get any for these samples.” I think these are related.

“Or could the reason for nonsense CNV detection results be in faulty GC content calculation and thus in the normalization after that? Because I'm not sure I understood what should be changed for mtDNA analysis in that function.” You might not need to change anything. I was recommending a sanity check. For example, calculating the GC content for the mt targets using the (modified) codex code and then compare it with those from for example the UCSC genome browser.

I hope that these are helpful. If you need further help, please use save.image(file=‘mt.debug.rda’) and send me the image file with specific questions.

Cheers,
Yuchao
